newsitem.title: UK: Man sees slower decline in world sugar prices.
newsitem.headline: Man sees slower decline in world sugar prices.

text.p: World sugar prices should retain their bearish stance, pressured by a large global surplus, but the fall is likely to be hesitant, E D & F Man said on Tuesday.

In its latest monthly report, Man said the market had seen technically-inspired support which had generated a certain resilience, partly explaining why prices had not fallen as much as statistics might indicate.

"Outright prices are set to remain under pressure although with the possibility of an increase in the EU C carry forward reducing the overall volume of exportable surplus and the delayed start of the Cuban production, this prosepctive fall in prices is likely to be hesitant," it said.
"The negative implications for the whites trade surplus may be tempered by the EU producers opting to expand their surplus C carry."
The Cuban crop was widely rumoured to be lower than generally anticipated previously and estimates for this year's Thai crop were moving down to levels similar to last year, it added.

But Man noted that the cancellation of the first additional 200,000-tonne tranche of the U.S. import quota after the release of January's supply/demand figures would release sugar onto the world market which had previously been earmarked for the U.S. -- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
